codeReview.summary: The dedicated IPC branch fixes command latency, but the loop now recreates the poll timer every iteration, so sustained IPC traffic can indefinitely delay daemon_tick and violate the expected poll cadence.

issues.description: Using `tokio::time::sleep(poll_interval)` directly inside `tokio::select!` recreates a fresh sleep future after every handled IPC command. If IPC commands keep arriving faster than `poll_interval`, the sleep arm never reaches completion, so `daemon_tick` can be starved and no longer fire at poll cadence.

The new tests validate a simulated select loop (`run_select_loop`) instead of the production `run_daemon` loop. This means a future regression in daemon loop wiring could pass these tests unless an integration test asserts tick cadence while IPC is active against production behavior.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Shared docs do not call out the async-loop pitfall that per-iteration `sleep()` in `select!` can starve periodic work under hot channels; this regression pattern is currently undocumented.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: AGENTS.md and .factory/library/architecture.md describe daemon polling at a high level, but there is no guidance to use a persistent timer/interval for cadence-sensitive branches.

summary: Review failed due to a blocking cadence regression risk: daemon_tick can be starved under sustained IPC traffic because the sleep timer is reset after each received command.
